description: Golden reference for calc_accel_magnet.py on the C-type dipole em_sample.jou (half-z model, linear mu_r=1000).
rationale: Knowledge accumulation mechanism (per user feedback 2026-04-24 about losing working implementations): locks the end-to-end path yoke.jou -> radia_export netgen (with Auto-Kelvin quarter-detected -> full z-cut kelvin pair) -> NGSolve Mesh + BBBND GND via CD3 propagation -> FEM Omega-reduced + Kelvin periodic -> B_origin + W_mag + L.  Any regression in the Cubit plugin's nodeset/sideset export, in add_periodic_kelvin fallback, or in calc_accel_magnet's Dirichlet setup will trip this test.

sample.generator_cmd_note: Regenerate via Cubit batch: python-run em_sample.jou + auto_add_kelvin_from_current_model() + radia_export netgen order=1 overwrite.  Reference template: C:/temp/run_em_sample.py (session work 2026-04-24).

geometry_note: Half-y model: yoke in y=[0, 0.18] only (no y-reflection in mesh; physically the ELF reference is quarter-XZ with mesh reduced further).  Comparing to the ELF quarter-XZ -976 mT reference requires setting up sym_tangential/sym_normal BCs and matching the Radia image decomposition -- that variant lives in the future corpus entries em/em_1-4_quarter_xz.jou etc.

expected_linear.note: Linearity check: since calc_accel_magnet has no non-linear BH with --material linear, B is exactly proportional to the coil current.  Run with coil_script=.step gives current=1.0 (hardcoded in to_coil_builder); the .py coil script bakes current=NI=2000.  Each row here is an observation used as a regression guard, NOT a match to ELF CEFC 2020 reference (-976 mT @ NI=2000 mu_r=1000) which is a quarter-XZ Radia-MSC result on a different mesh discretization.

I_2000A_coil_py.note: Should be exactly 2000x the I_1A B values; L should be identical (geometry-only).
